title: Read the Loop
blurb: The bread and butter: look at a small piece of code and name its worst-case time complexity. Constants and lower-order terms don't matter — only how the work grows with n.

levels.title: L1 · Constant work
levels.hint: Is there a loop at all? How much work happens regardless of the array size?
levels.explain: There’s no loop — indexing an array is one fixed operation no matter how big the array is. That’s O(1).

failStates.title: No loop — just one access
failStates.explain: Indexing an array is a single operation regardless of how big the array is. No matter the size, it does the same fixed work → O(1).

levels.title: L2 · A single loop
levels.hint: How many times does the body run, relative to n?

blocks.label: Code

levels.explain: The body runs once per element, n times total, so the cost scales directly with n: O(n).

failStates.title: The work depends on n
failStates.explain: The body runs once per element — n times total. Since the work grows with the input, it's O(n), not constant.

failStates.title: Only one loop here
failStates.explain: O(n²) needs a loop inside a loop. This is a single pass → O(n).

levels.title: L3 · Steps of size k
levels.prompt: k is a constant. What is the time complexity?
levels.hint: Does a constant step size change the ORDER of growth, or just a constant factor?

blocks.label: Code

levels.explain: Stepping by a constant k runs the loop n/k times; drop the constant and it’s still O(n). Adding to the loop variable keeps it linear.

failStates.title: Adding a constant is still linear
failStates.explain: Stepping by k runs the loop n/k times. Dropping the constant 1/k, that's still O(n). You'd only get O(log n) if you multiplied or divided x each step, not added to it.

failStates.title: It still scales with n
failStates.explain: n/k iterations grows as n grows, so it's not constant — it's O(n).

levels.title: L4 · Nested loops
levels.prompt: Both loops run over the same array. What is the time complexity?
levels.hint: Multiply the outer loop’s iterations by the inner loop’s.

blocks.label: Code

levels.explain: Two nested loops, each running n times: n × n = O(n²).

failStates.title: Two nested loops multiply
failStates.explain: For each of the n outer iterations, the inner loop runs n times: n × n = n² total → O(n²).

failStates.title: No halving here
failStates.explain: n log n comes from divide-and-conquer (like sorting). Both of these loops are linear and nested, so it's O(n²).

levels.title: L5 · The shrinking inner loop
levels.prompt: The inner loop starts at i, so it shrinks. What is the time complexity?
levels.hint: The inner loop shrinks — add up n + (n−1) + … + 1. What does that sum grow like?

blocks.label: Code

levels.explain: The inner loop shrinks, but n + (n−1) + … + 1 = n(n+1)/2 ≈ n²/2. Drop the ½ and it’s still O(n²) — half of quadratic is quadratic.

failStates.title: A shrinking inner loop is still quadratic
failStates.explain: The inner loop runs n, then n−1, then n−2 … totalling n(n+1)/2 ≈ n²/2. Drop the constant ½ → O(n²). Half of n² is still quadratic.

levels.title: L6 · Divide each step
levels.prompt: Look at how i changes. What is the time complexity?
levels.hint: Is i decremented or divided each step? That’s the difference between linear and logarithmic.

blocks.label: Code

levels.explain: i is halved each step (n → n/2 → … → 1), which happens only about log₂(n) times: O(log n). Dividing the loop variable by a constant is the signature of logarithmic time.

failStates.title: It's halved, not decremented
failStates.explain: i goes n → n/2 → n/4 → … → 1. That's only about log₂(n) steps, not n. Dividing (or multiplying) the loop variable by a constant is the signature of O(log n).

failStates.title: It still depends on n
failStates.explain: It runs log n times — which grows (slowly) as n grows — so it isn't constant. It's O(log n).

levels.title: L7 · Looks nested, but…
levels.prompt: The inner loop advances the OUTER index i. What is the time complexity?
levels.hint: Count how many times the innermost line runs in total — watch what happens to i inside the loop.

blocks.label: Code

levels.explain: It looks nested, but the inner loop advances the outer index i, so i goes 0→n only once across the whole run — the body executes ~n times total: O(n). Always count how many times the innermost line runs, not how many loops are stacked.

failStates.title: The gotcha: count total iterations, not nesting
failStates.explain: It LOOKS like O(n²), but the inner loop increments i — the outer index. Across the whole run, i advances from 0 to n exactly once, so the body runs about n times total → O(n). Always count how many times the innermost line actually runs, not how many loops are stacked.
